column2: The museum offered a compelling reason to visit: a rare manuscript displayed for the first time.
column3: 博物館提供了令人信服的參觀理由：一份首度展出的珍貴手稿。
column4: a compelling argument (令人信服的論點)
column5: com 一起 + pel 推：推得你不得不點頭、不得不看
column8: 令人信服的；強烈吸引人的

column2: Her cogent essay linked each claim to evidence, leaving the examiners no reason to doubt it.
column3: 她論證嚴密的文章把每項主張都連結到證據，讓考官沒有理由懷疑。
column5: 諧音「口缺」：口才一點缺口也沒有，論證嚴密
column8: 論證嚴密的；有說服力的

column2: The cogency of the report came from its careful data and clear logic.
column3: 這份報告的說服力來自嚴謹的資料與清晰的邏輯。
column4: cogency of an argument (論證的嚴密性)
column5: cogent 加 -cy 變名詞：論據扎實不鬆動

column2: The lucidity of the teacher's explanation made the hardest chapter feel simple to every student.
column3: 老師解說的清晰條理，讓最難的一章對每位學生來說都變簡單了。
column5: luc 光：像燈亮起來，一切都看得清楚

column2: Cognitive scientists test how young children learn language by watching how they solve simple puzzles.
column3: 認知科學家透過觀察幼童如何解簡單謎題，來檢驗他們如何學習語言。
column5: 諧音「寇格尼提夫」：頭腦裡思考、理解的歷程
column8: 認知的；思考歷程的；知覺的

column2: Research suggests that regular exercise can slow the decline of cognition in older adults.
column3: 研究顯示，規律運動可減緩老年人認知能力的衰退。
column5: co 一起 + gnition 知道：腦袋知道、了解事物的能力

column2: Her perception of the city changed after she lived there for a year and met its people.
column3: 在城裡住了一年並認識當地人之後，她對這座城市的看法改變了。
column5: per 透過 + ception 接收：用感官接收到的看法

column2: His apprehension grew as the exam hall filled up and the clock began to tick.
column3: 隨著考場坐滿人、時鐘開始滴答作響，他的焦慮愈來愈強。
column5: ap 去 + prehend 抓：心被抓住，放不下

column2: The apprehensive young actor paced backstage, whispering his lines before the curtain rose.
column3: 緊張不安的年輕演員在後台踱步，在布幕升起前低聲唸著台詞。
column5: apprehension 的形容詞：心一直被抓著不放

column2: A reporter's bias can shape which facts appear in the first paragraph of a story.
column3: 記者的偏見會影響哪些事實被放進報導的第一段。
column5: 諧音「拜亞斯」：拜一邊、歪一邊，天秤歪斜
column8: 偏見；成見；偏袒；使有偏向

column2: The judge removed the biased juror, who had already decided the defendant was guilty.
column3: 法官撤換了有偏見的陪審員，他早已認定被告有罪。
column5: bias 加 ed：已經歪向一邊的

column2: Prejudice against newcomers made it hard for the family to find work in the small town.
column3: 對新來者的偏見，使這家人在小鎮上很難找到工作。
column5: pre 先 + judice 判斷：還沒了解就先判了
column8: 先入之見；成見；偏見；抱偏見

column2: Whether a painting is beautiful is a subjective matter; ten critics may give ten different answers.
column3: 畫作美不美是主觀的問題，十位評論家可能給出十種不同答案。
column5: subject 主體：從「我自己」的角度看出去

column2: The subjectivity of memory means two siblings may recall the same afternoon very differently.
column3: 記憶的主觀性意味著兩個手足可能對同一個下午有截然不同的回憶。
column5: subjective 變名詞：每個人心裡一把尺

column2: A scientist should remain objective and report the results even when they disappoint her.
column3: 科學家應保持客觀，即使結果令她失望也要如實報告。
column5: object 物體：像看桌上的東西，不加入自己的情感
column8: 客觀的；客觀標準的；目標；方針

column2: The anchor praised the panel for its objectivity, since it examined both sides without taking sides.
column3: 主播稱讚小組的客觀公正，因為它檢視雙方而不偏袒任何一方。
column5: objective 變名詞：像相機鏡頭只照實景

column2: Healthy skepticism led the historian to check the diary against three other sources.
column3: 健康的懷疑態度讓歷史學家拿日記去對照另外三份資料。
column5: 諧音「死計提洗」：先思考一下，別馬上相信
column8: 懷疑論；懷疑態度；質疑心

column2: The skeptical farmer doubted the salesman's promise that the new seeds would double his harvest.
column3: 存疑的農夫不相信推銷員所說新種子能讓收成加倍的承諾。
column5: skeptic 加 al：眉毛一挑，「真的嗎？」

column2: Years of broken promises had bred a deep cynicism about politics among the young voters.
column3: 多年來被打破的承諾，讓年輕選民對政治生出深深的憤世嫉俗。
column4: political cynicism (對政治的犬儒心態)
column5: cyn 像 dog 犬：古希臘犬儒派，對什麼都冷笑
column8: 憤世嫉俗；諷刺；犬儒心態

column2: He gave a cynical laugh, convinced that every charity secretly wanted only publicity.
column3: 他發出憤世嫉俗的笑聲，深信每個慈善機構暗地裡只想要宣傳。
column5: cynicism 的形容詞：覺得人人都自私
column8: 犬儒的；憤世嫉俗的；覺得人自私的

column2: She felt ambivalence about moving abroad, thrilled by the adventure yet saddened to leave her family.
column3: 她對出國感到矛盾，既為冒險而興奮，又為離開家人而難過。
column5: ambi 兩邊 + valence 力量：兩邊同時拉扯你
column8: 矛盾情感；正反兩念交織

column2: Voters' indifference to the local election resulted in barely twenty percent turning out to vote.
column3: 選民對地方選舉的漠不關心，使得只有約兩成的人出來投票。
column5: in 不 + different 差別：什麼都沒差，無所謂

column2: He remained indifferent to the cheering crowd and kept his eyes on the finish line.
column3: 他對歡呼的群眾不為所動，目光始終盯著終點線。
column4: indifferent to praise (對讚美無動於衷)
column5: in 不 + different 有差別：沒差，我無所謂

column2: Widespread apathy among citizens allowed the corrupt council to remain in office for decades.
column3: 公民之間普遍的冷漠，使腐敗的議會得以連任數十年。
column5: a 無 + pathy 感受：對什麼都沒感覺
column8: 漠不關心；無同情心；消極

column2: The apathetic student stared out the window and never raised his hand all term.
column3: 冷漠的學生望著窗外，整個學期從未舉手。
column5: apathy 的形容詞：像一尊沒反應的石像
column8: 缺乏興趣的；冷漠的；麻木的

column2: Her empathy let her understand the lonely boy's pain without his saying a word.
column3: 她的同理心，讓她不必他開口就能體會那個孤單男孩的痛苦。
column5: em 進入 + pathy 感受：走進對方的心裡
column8: 同理心；感同身受的能力

column2: The nurse's empathic listening made frightened patients feel truly understood.
column3: 護理師富有同理心的傾聽，讓害怕的病人感到真正被理解。
column4: empathic listener (有同理心的傾聽者)
column5: empathy 的形容詞：心有靈犀、能共鳴
column8: 富同理心的；深具共鳴的

column2: The mayor sent a letter of sympathy to the families who had lost their homes in the flood.
column3: 市長寄信向在洪水中失去家園的家庭致上慰問。
column5: sym 一起 + pathy 感受：陪你一起難過

column2: Moved by compassion, the stranger shared his coat with the shivering child.
column3: 出於悲憫，陌生人把外套分給發抖的孩子。
column5: com 一起 + passion 感受：與人同感，想伸出手

column2: A compassionate teacher, she stayed late each day to help students who were falling behind.
column3: 身為富有同情心的老師，她每天留到很晚，幫助跟不上的學生。
column5: compassion 加 ate：心裡滿滿的溫柔

column2: His reluctance to speak in public came from a bad memory of forgetting his lines.
column3: 他不願公開演講，源自一次忘詞的糟糕回憶。
column5: re 向後 + luct 掙扎：身體往後縮，不想去

column2: The reluctant swimmer dipped one toe in the icy lake and stepped back.
column3: 不情願的游泳者把一根腳趾伸進冰冷的湖水，又退了回來。
column5: reluctance 的形容詞：腳往後退，心不想去
column8: 不情願的；勉強的；抗拒的

column2: She was hesitant to sign the contract until her lawyer had read every page.
column3: 在律師讀完每一頁之前，她遲疑著不肯簽約。
column5: hes 黏住：腳像被黏住，一步也走不出去
column8: 猶豫的；遲疑的；遲疑不決的

column2: After a moment of hesitation, the diver stepped off the edge and into the cold water.
column3: 遲疑片刻之後，潛水員從岸邊一步跨入冰冷的水中。
column5: hesitant 變名詞：黏住了，停了一下

column2: The young volunteers worked with ardor, painting the entire school fence in a single weekend.
column3: 年輕志工們熱情十足地工作，一個週末就漆完了整座學校圍牆。
column5: ard 像 hard 燃燒：心裡像火在燒的熱情

column2: An ardent supporter of the team, he attended every match in snow, rain, and heat.
column3: 身為球隊的熱情支持者，他不論風雪、下雨或酷暑都出席每一場比賽。
column5: ardor 的形容詞：心中有一團熊熊火焰

column2: The preacher's fervor filled the hall, and the crowd began to clap and sing.
column3: 傳教士的熱情充滿大廳，群眾開始鼓掌歌唱。
column5: ferv 沸騰：像水燒開咕嚕咕嚕冒泡的熱情

column2: She made a fervent plea for more funds to save the old library from closing.
column3: 她熱切地呼籲增加經費，以免老圖書館關閉。
column5: fervor 的形容詞：滾燙沸騰的心意

column2: With great zeal, the young reformer visited every village to promote clean water.
column3: 年輕的改革者滿懷熱忱，走訪每座村莊推廣潔淨飲水。
column5: 諧音「 ZEAL 滋」：熱情滋滋冒，燃燒到停不下來

column2: The zealous volunteers cleaned the beach every morning, rain or shine, for an entire year.
column3: 熱心的志工們整整一年，不論晴雨，每天早晨都在清理海灘。
column5: zeal 加 ous：熱忱滿滿、停不下來的人
